significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that factual hallucination probability increases as "the magnitude of enrichment (locus state norm/probe strength)" decreases, with near-baseline enrichment for unseen entities and better prediction than output entropy; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between independently measurable internal strength and subsequent error. It would constrain expectations for unknown entities and separate retrieval-absence cases from "strong-but-wrong retrieval," informing whether uncertainty methods such as Kuhn et al.'s semantic-entropy approach are measuring the same failure mechanism or a different one. The claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic explanation—"hallucination is the absence of retrieval, not corrupted retrieval"—while a negative result would meaningfully reject that explanation as the dominant account; true and false are distinguishable through the stated directional and comparative predictions, although "dominates" lacks a quantitative threshold. In the topic-substitution check, generic questions about why stored knowledge fails would not merit this score; the added enrichment-error coupling and two-mode decomposition are the claim-specific reasons it rises above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "magnitude of enrichment (locus state norm/probe strength)," proposed as a "cheap, single-forward-pass detector" and as a discriminator between absent retrieval and strong-but-wrong retrieval. Because the signal is read at the subject recall locus, it is potentially ex ante—available before the factual answer is completed—giving auditors or decoding systems an action window rather than merely explaining a false answer afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a transferable directional relation—weak enrichment should forecast hallucination and unseen entities should approach baseline—rather than merely supplying a search procedure, although the stated scope is chiefly factual QA and the claim explicitly leaves long-form generation uncertain. The downstream users could include model auditors and deployment systems that gate or mitigate low-enrichment answers; deleting this specific detector and retaining only the broad knowledge-retrieval topic would not support the score, so the topic-substitution check passes.
